title: DeepSeek Is Said to Report to the UN Security Council About the Potential Risks and Security Challenges of AI
excerpt: The rapid development of artificial intelligence technology is accelerating from mere industrial competition to a core issue of global security and geopolitics.
content_html:
The rapid development of artificial intelligence technology is accelerating from mere industrial competition to a core issue of global security and geopolitics. According to a report by Reuters citing informed sources, the Chinese AI startup DeepSeek is expected to provide a special briefing to the United Nations Security Council this week on the potential risks and security challenges posed by artificial intelligence.

As a globally watched frontier AI force, DeepSeek's invitation to participate in the UN Security Council's security briefing reflects the international community's recognition of the substantial role Chinese large model companies play in technological governance, risk prevention, and the construction of global AI safety frameworks. At the same time, other Chinese AI companies, such as Moonshot AI supported by Alibaba, are also gradually stepping onto the international stage, jointly exploring how to address long-term challenges brought by general artificial intelligence on a global scale.

As major AI laboratories continue to push the boundaries with technological iterations, balancing technological innovation with safety red lines has become an urgent priority for global multilateral governance mechanisms. DeepSeek's participation in the UN Security Council to share its insights and practices on AI risks not only provides a technical perspective from a Chinese tech company to the international community, but also marks a new phase in global AI governance, moving towards more multilateral cooperation and in-depth dialogue.
